subject: Acme Pay — request for subprocessor proof and DPA scope clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@acmepay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Request: subprocessor inventory + DPA clause question

Hi Ben / Kimberly,

Following our procurement review, Acme Pay needs an up-to-date inventory of all subprocessors that will process Acme customer data for the Redwood service used in our pilot. In addition, legal flagged a DPA point: we need confirmation whether any of those subprocessors will perform cross-border transfers outside the US/EU and whether Redwood intends to add a new onboarding clause for short-lived temporary processors (e.g., analytics relays).

Can you provide: 1) a spreadsheet listing current subprocessors, location/jurisdiction, and role; 2) any planned additions in the next 90 days; 3) whether Redwood is proposing a DPA amendment for temporary processors or if those are covered by existing language?

We have a soft deadline of Friday (9/8) to keep our procurement timeline. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Legal — Acme Pay
Elena.Morales@acmepay.com

Quick note on process: we maintain a live subprocessor inventory and can export the current roster with jurisdictions and roles. Jonas (legal) and Kimberly (security & privacy) are looped in to provide the export and the DPA guidance.

Jonas / Kimberly — can you confirm if the current inventory and our standard DPA cover temporary analytics relays, or if we should provide an explicit clause or amendment for Acme? Also: Ben asked for a 90-day plan column — is there any anticipated onboarding in that window?

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Sep 2028 09:28:00 -0400
Subject: FW: Request: subprocessor inventory + DPA clause question

Ben / Kimberly — forwarding the initial request and attaching a working export.

Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_inventory_v3.xlsx (columns: processor_name, role, primary_jurisdiction, data_types_processed, contract_signed_date, expected_change_window)
Attachment: dpa_amendment_draft_comments.pdf (internal draft with paragraph suggestions)

Notes:
- Current roster does include a handful of temporary analytics relays (used for ephemeral telemetry) that are engaged under our standard subprocessor governance and addendum process. They are not currently named in the DPA explicitly; instead, the DPA references subprocessors in scope with the ability to notify customers of additions.
- For customers requiring a stricter carveout (onshore-only or explicit naming), we typically provide an export + attestation and propose either: 
  a) a narrow DPA addendum enumerating those temporary relays, or
  b) a contractual attestation that no temporary relays process Acme Pay data outside approved jurisdictions.

I recommend option (b) as a faster path unless Acme prefers explicit naming (a). If we go with (a) we should re-run procurement redlines.

Will add brief comments in the PDF and can prepare a cleaned export for Acme — want to confirm scope first (prod vs test data).

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Hi Elena — looping back with specific questions so we can produce the right export and language.

1) Scope: do you need the roster to include temporary test/QA relays or only production processors?
2) Residency tolerance: is Acme okay with processors based in the UK and CA (we map both as 'eu-like' jurisdictions), or do you require strictly US/EU (EU27) residency?
3) If we provide a DPA attestation (option b from Jonas), would Acme need any additional audit evidence (SOC2 snapshot, configuration screenshots) attached to that attestation?

We attached an annotated export internally; I'll prepare a customer-facing CSV and a short attestation template for your review.

Forwarding your original note below for context.

--

From: Elena Morales <elena@acmepay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Sep 2028 09:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor inventory + DPA clause question

Thanks — answers below and appreciate the fast turnaround.

1) Please include production processors only. QA/test relays are not required.
2) Residency: Acme legal will accept UK and Canada as long as there is documented contractual and technical controls (encryption at rest, access controls) and no onward transfers outside those jurisdictions without notice.
3) Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II snapshot and a short configuration screenshot (shows regional routing settings) would be sufficient. We do not require full escrow or HSM evidence at this stage.

Next steps: can Redwood provide the production-only CSV + an attestation statement saying no temporary relays process Acme customer data outside of approved jurisdictions, plus the SOC2 snapshot? If you can get that over by EOD Friday (9/8), we can keep the procurement timeline.

Elena
Legal — Acme Pay
